summary.intent: Prepare a Hacker News-ready article and supporting docs/pages for Caliper (React docgen tool using oxc + the tsrs checker), and bring the pages-site evidence pages (parity, measurement, main Caliper page) and both repos' docs in line with verified, honestly-caveated findings.
summary.outcome: Parallel readers produced verified PR ledgers and an ADR 0026 fact sheet; the pages site gained a shared dated data module, a rebuilt measurement page with speed and memory ratios, a chapter-list TOC via DocumentPage, fixed prev/next cards, and new z-index tokens. The pages docs and four Caliper docs were updated, with a signed local commit on a worktree branch. Nothing is pushed or committed in the pages repo, and the article itself is not yet drafted.

repo: ADR 0026: the checker (tsrs) decides types and oxc decides syntax. The structural resolver is a fallback marked with `degradedBy`. tsrs is pinned to an exact build, and the weekly oracle keeps the Go checker so it never grades itself.
The default has not flipped to checker-first (S8 not done). S4 'checker wins' is done but one gate failed: the Storybook first answer on a large project took 402-562 ms against a 150 ms target.

Most PRs #329-#363 have empty Entire shadow-PR boilerplate bodies, so substance lives in commit bodies, changesets and docs/measurement.md. Stacked PRs repeatedly merged into parent branches out of order.

The weekly record counts (component, prop) pairs; a prop shared across 700 components counts 700 times. RDT is scored over every function it lists, including non-components, while Caliper is scored only over reported components. Counts are shown as count plus share of listed props.
On share, Caliper is worse than RDT on Mantine, React Spectrum and Ant Design for 'less precise', and better only on shadcn/ui and Chakra.

Nov 9 weekly CI record: Caliper is 16-66x faster than RDT (median 22x) and uses 2.5-5.8x less memory (median 4x). Caliper time is a median of 5 runs and RDT's is a single run. The October 28x figure was a laptop run and must not be mixed with CI numbers.
Pages repo: tool pages use the system's DocumentPage (chapter rail, footer slot for PageSequence). Sections need width='frame' with a spacing wrapper, and the footer wrapper needs data-reading.

Pages repo z-index tokens: added zIndex.rail (1) and zIndex.trail (2) to both brands. The chapter list used a literal 1 and the breadcrumb borrowed toggle.raised (also 1), so the list covered the trail's open menu. Site nav still uses literal 10/11 in siteNavParts.ts.
The Caliper worktree has no node_modules, so oxfmt was run using the main checkout's binary. The Caliper repo requires planning a trail before branches and asking before any push or PR.
docs/STATUS.md (dated 2026-11-02), docs/measurement.md, docs/performance.md and the README were stale or contradicted the pages, and apps/orin-dx-docs has no Caliper pages.

code.finding: Design: the checker decides types and oxc decides syntax. oxc re-applies union member order and the structural fallback carries degradedBy. The pin policy requires the construct suite plus a tsrs-vs-Go parity run. In-process linking via tsrs_api::Session was rejected (publish=false, no process isolation, no restart lever).
S4 is marked 'done, one gate failed'. The addon keeps structural-first inside a semanticWaitMs window because the checker is too slow for first paint.
New shared typed module holding the Nov 9 weekly record with its date. The parity, measurement and main Caliper pages and the family metrics all read from it so figures can't drift.
Rewritten to wrap evidence pages in DocumentPage, with the trail above the document and the hero as the lead.

friction: Read-agent reports were truncated mid-ledger and needed resend requests.
Many PR bodies are empty shells, so figures had to be recovered from commits and docs, and the trail findings were never read.
Initial width='text' sections spilled across the chapter rail, and the DocumentPage conversion broke the prev/next cards (they ran edge to edge) and moved source notes after section content.
Lint and typecheck failures along the way: a wrong chapter-type import path, numeric separators, and a foundations build exit 1 caused by a missing task.
A z-index collision from a literal 1 and a borrowed token hid the breadcrumb menu.
The Caliper worktree lacked node_modules, so pnpm tried the registry, and the new tables needed formatter alignment.
The user's earlier 'agent said it wasn't so right' caveat about counts couldn't be located in the transcript.
open_items: Draft the Hacker News article and claims ledger once the remaining readers (read-prs-b rest, read-entire, read-docs rest, read-tsrs) report, and decide timing (publish at the decision point vs after S8).
